# ui::Palette

Header: `winui/ui/themes/Palette.hpp`.

The Fluent colors a [Theme](theme.md) is derived from, one field per role: text, control fills, strokes, accent, surfaces and status colors.

[Theme::fluent()](theme.md#fluent) derives every control's colors from a Palette. [fluent_light()](#fluent_light) and [fluent_dark()](#fluent_dark) give the Windows 11 colors, and [fluent1_light()](#fluent1_light) and [fluent1_dark()](#fluent1_dark) the Windows 10 ones. A custom palette starts from one of them and changes fields. A Palette is plain data and cheap to copy.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Palette palette = ui::Palette::fluent_dark();
palette.accent_fill_default = ui::Color::from_argb(0xFF8764B8); // a purple accent
palette.accent_text_primary = ui::Color::from_argb(0xFFD4C3F0);

ui::Theme theme = ui::Theme::fluent(palette);
window.pin_theme(std::move(theme)); // accent buttons, toggles and links now use the purple
```

## dark

```cpp
bool dark = false
```

Whether this is a dark palette. A few shapes differ between light and dark, and [`Theme::fluent()`](theme.md#fluent) reads them from this flag. The main one is the neutral elevation border, whose gradient is flipped vertically in light and not in dark. Set by the factories, and false in a default-constructed Palette.

## control_fill_input_active

```cpp
Color control_fill_input_active
```

A focused text field ([TextBox](../controls/text-box.md#uitextbox), [PasswordBox](../controls/password-box.md#uipasswordbox), [RichEditBox](../controls/rich-edit-box.md#uiricheditbox), [AutoSuggestBox](../controls/auto-suggest-box.md#uiautosuggestbox), [NumberBox](../controls/number-box.md#uinumberbox)). The one opaque fill of this set in light, so the field turns from a translucent wash into a solid surface on focus. Light's is plain white, which differs from [`solid_background_tertiary`](#solid_background_tertiary)'s `#F9F9F9`.

## control_alt_fill_secondary

```cpp
Color control_alt_fill_secondary
```

The fill of an unchecked [CheckBox](../controls/check-box.md#uicheckbox), [RadioButton](../controls/radio-button.md#uiradiobutton) or [ToggleSwitch](../controls/toggle-switch.md#uitoggleswitch) indicator at rest, a slightly recessed surface distinct from `control_fill_*`. The three `control_alt_fill_*` fields after it are hover, pressed and disabled. Three values are easy to guess wrong:
- Dark's rest fill is translucent black (`#19000000`), so a dark unchecked box at rest is darker than the page.
- In light, rest is the fainter 2 % wash and hover the 6 % one.
- The disabled fill is transparent in both themes, so a disabled box shows only its stroke.

## on_backdrop_hover

```cpp
Color on_backdrop_hover
```

A control sitting directly on the window's Mica backdrop, such as a tab of a [Tabs](../controls/tabs.md#uitabs) control, under the pointer. It replaces the `subtle_fill_*` colors there. The pressed fill is a lighter, mostly opaque layer (light 0xB3FFFFFF, dark 0x733A3A3A), so a tab brightens on press. At rest the control is transparent, which needs no field.

## on_backdrop_pressed

```cpp
Color on_backdrop_pressed
```

That control pressed.

## accent_fill_default

```cpp
Color accent_fill_default
```

Accent buttons, checked toggles and selection indicators. The value is the default accent. A [Theme](theme.md) resolved from the OS replaces it with the user's accent.

## accent_fill_disabled

```cpp
Color accent_fill_disabled
```

An accent-filled control while disabled, a neutral wash.

## accent_text_primary

```cpp
Color accent_text_primary
```

Link text at rest. The four `accent_text_*` fields cover rest, hover, pressed and disabled link text. They use other shades of the accent than the fill above: in light, rest, hover and pressed are [`AccentRamp::dark2`](accent-ramp.md), `dark3` and `dark1`, and in dark they are `light3`, `light3` and `light2`. Windows 10 has no such shades, so [fluent1_light()](#fluent1_light) and [fluent1_dark()](#fluent1_dark) fill these with its own link colors.

## control_stroke_on_accent_default

```cpp
Color control_stroke_on_accent_default
```

The first stop of an accent control's elevation-border gradient. This pair differs from the neutral [`control_stroke_default`](#control_stroke_default) and [`control_stroke_secondary`](#control_stroke_secondary). The second stop is a 40 % black hairline in light, against the neutral 16 %, and this one is translucent white in both themes, where the neutral one flips between black and white.

## control_stroke_on_accent_secondary

```cpp
Color control_stroke_on_accent_secondary
```

The second stop of that gradient, the darker edge of an accent control.

## control_strong_stroke_default

```cpp
Color control_strong_stroke_default
```

The border of an unchecked [CheckBox](../controls/check-box.md#uicheckbox), [RadioButton](../controls/radio-button.md#uiradiobutton) or [ToggleSwitch](../controls/toggle-switch.md#uitoggleswitch). It is much bolder than [`control_stroke_default`](#control_stroke_default), so an unchecked toggle still looks interactive.

## surface_stroke_default

```cpp

```

The 1px frame of a surface that floats over the page, such as [TeachingTip](../controls/teaching-tip.md#uiteachingtip). The same `#66757575` in light and dark.

## layer_fill_alt

```cpp

```

The top area of a [DialogControl](../controls/dialog.md#uidialogcontrol), opaque white in light and a 5 % white wash in dark. Transparent in the Windows 10 palettes.

```cpp

```

A control drawn over a picture, such as the unchecked multi-select box of a TileViewItem. This field and the three after it are rest, hover, pressed and disabled: light `#C9FFFFFF`, `#F3F3F3`, `#EBEBEB` and `#00FFFFFF`, dark `#B31C1C1C`, `#1A1A1A`, `#131313` and `#1E1E1E`.

## acrylic_fallback_default

```cpp
Color acrylic_fallback_default
```

The solid color of the in-app acrylic material: `#2C2C2C` in dark, `#F9F9F9` in light. Popups that close on an outside click, such as menus, flyouts, the [ComboBox](../controls/combo-box.md#uicombobox) list and [ToolTip](../controls/tool-tip.md#uitooltip), draw in acrylic. This color replaces the acrylic whenever it is off: with transparency effects disabled, in battery saver, on a low-end GPU or in high contrast. Both values match the Windows 11 system popup menu. In dark it differs from [`solid_background_tertiary`](#solid_background_tertiary) (`#282828`).

## card_background_default

```cpp
Color card_background_default
```

The fill of a card surface, such as an [Expander](../layout/expander.md#uiexpander)'s header, paired with [`card_stroke_default`](#card_stroke_default). 0xB3FFFFFF in light, 0x0DFFFFFF in dark, where [`control_fill_default`](#control_fill_default) is 0x0FFFFFFF.

## card_background_secondary

```cpp
Color card_background_secondary
```

A card's recessed inner region, such as an expanded [Expander](../layout/expander.md#uiexpander)'s content panel.

## semantic_fill_success

```cpp
Color semantic_fill_success
```

The success icon of an [InfoBar](../controls/info-bar.md#uiinfobar) and a success [InfoBadge](../controls/info-badge.md#uiinfobadge). The `semantic_fill_*` colors are strong marks for icons and badges. The `semantic_background_*` colors are the much fainter washes that fill an [InfoBar](../controls/info-bar.md#uiinfobar)'s body. The informational severity has no fill color because its icon uses the accent, so [InfoBar](../controls/info-bar.md#uiinfobar) reads [`accent_fill_default`](#accent_fill_default) for it.


## tabular_header_background

```cpp
Color tabular_header_background
```

The header band of tabular controls such as [TableView](../controls/table-view.md#uitableview). A translucent wash of about 15 % alpha, above [`control_stroke_default`](#control_stroke_default)'s 6 to 7 %, so it stands out over row banding.

## tabular_grid_line

```cpp
Color tabular_grid_line
```

The gridlines between rows and cells of tabular controls, stronger than [`divider_stroke_default`](#divider_stroke_default) so they stay visible at 1px over alternating rows.

## tabular_row_alternating

```cpp
Color tabular_row_alternating
```

Every second row of a tabular control with banding on. It has the same values as [`subtle_fill_secondary`](#subtle_fill_secondary).

## acrylic_in_app_default

```cpp
AcrylicBrush acrylic_in_app_default() const
```

The in-app acrylic material as an [AcrylicBrush](../rendering/acrylic-brush.md). Light has tint `#FCFCFC` at opacity 0 and luminosity opacity 0.85, dark has `#2C2C2C` at 0.15 and 0.96, and both fall back to [`acrylic_fallback_default`](#acrylic_fallback_default). Drawn with [Renderer::draw_geometry()](../rendering/renderer.md#draw_geometry), it blurs what is behind it.

## fluent_light

```cpp
static Palette fluent_light()
```

The Windows 11 light colors. The accent fields hold shades of the default accent (`#005A9E` for the fill). A theme resolved from the OS replaces them with the user's accent.

## fluent_dark

```cpp
static Palette fluent_dark()
```

The Windows 11 dark colors, with the default accent's light shades (`#76B9ED` for the fill) in the accent fields.

## fluent1_light

```cpp
static Palette fluent1_light()
```

The Windows 10 light colors in the same roles: a pure white page, 20 % black button fills that lighten on hover, unfilled toggles, and the accent `#0078D4`.

## fluent1_dark

```cpp
static Palette fluent1_dark()
```

The Windows 10 dark colors. Its translucent text and fill colors are the exact inverse of [fluent1_light()](#fluent1_light)'s. Its opaque grays are not: they have their own order per theme, so a gray that is darker than another in light can be lighter in dark.
